record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Strong WARM percolation with bounded firing rates
record.original_question: For an infinite-graph WARM with reinforcement exponent alpha > 1 and firing rates p(v) bounded both away from zero and away from infinity, does the limit of every scaled edge weight X_e(t) exist almost surely, do the surviving edges form only finite connected components, and in the case alpha > 2 are those finite surviving components necessarily trees?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. Assume that firing rates p(v) are bounded away from zero and from infinity, and that α > 1. Then the limit limt→∞ Xe(t) exists almost surely for each e, and the surviving edges form finite connected components. In particular, for α > 2 they are trees.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be an infinite connected graph of bounded degree. Assign to each vertex v ∈ V a Poisson clock with rate p(v) > 0, where the firing rates are bounded away from 0 and from ∞ (i.e., there exist constants 0 < c ≤ C < ∞ such that c ≤ p(v) ≤ C for all v). Fix a reinforcement exponent α > 1. Define a continuous-time edge-reinforcement process (WARM) as follows: each edge e ∈ E has a weight X_e(t) starting at X_e(0) = 1; when the clock at vertex v rings at time t, one of the edges e incident to v is selected and its weight is incremented by 1, with the edge chosen with probability proportional to X_e(t−)^α among edges incident to v.

Let S_v(t) = Σ_{e ∋ v} X_e(t) and consider the scaled weights X_e(t) / (some natural normalization that makes the ratios converge), or equivalently, the long-run proportions of reinforcement on each edge. Call an edge e "surviving" if it is reinforced infinitely often as t → ∞.

Prove or disprove the following three assertions:

(a) For every edge e ∈ E, the limit lim_{t→∞} X_e(t)/t (or, equivalently, the appropriately scaled edge weight) exists almost surely.

(b) Almost surely, the subgraph formed by the surviving edges has only finite connected components.

(c) If moreover α > 2, then almost surely every connected component of the surviving-edge subgraph is a tree (i.e., contains no cycle).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in full generality. Partial progress exists: for sufficiently large α (very strong reinforcement), absence of percolation and the tree property of surviving components have been established (Hirsch–Holmes–Kleptsyn, "Infinite WARM graphs III: strong reinforcement regime", 2023, and related works on regular trees and Z^d). Results on a regular tree in the strong reinforcement regime and on phase transitions for constant firing rates are known, but the assertions for all α > 1 (finite components) and α > 2 (tree property) on arbitrary bounded-degree graphs are not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Infinite WARM graphs III: strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: Studies finite components in the strong reinforcement regime α > 1 with bounded clock rates; proves that for α sufficiently large all components are trees.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results: tree property and finiteness of components proven only for α sufficiently large, not for all α > 1.

status_evidence.title: WARM percolation on a regular tree in the strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: Studies WARM percolation on regular trees in the strong reinforcement regime α > 1.
status_evidence.claim: Special-case progress on regular trees, full conjecture remains open on general graphs.

status_evidence.title: Absence of WARM percolation in the very strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: Proves absence of WARM percolation in the very strong reinforcement regime.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes finiteness of components only in the very strong reinforcement regime, leaving the full α > 1 range open.
